FireSync 2026

Somos un equipo multidisciplinario integrado por Jano, Yuri, Valen, Siro y Mel. Nos apasiona profundamente la tecnología, la ciencia y el espacio, y este año participamos en el NASA Space Apps Challenge con un enfoque firme en la ciencia de datos, la investigación y el desarrollo tecnológico de alto nivel.
summary:
FireSync turns 26 years of NASA fire satellite data into one consistent record that anyone can explore. NASA's MODIS has mapped Earth's fires since 2000 and is retiring; its successor VIIRS sees fires differently (375 m pixels, 4–6× more hotspots), so joining the two raw records fakes a "fire explosion" in 2012. We processed all 556 million NASA FIRMS detections and harmonized them with a validated, stratified calibration (country × month × day/night) into VIIRS-equivalent hotspots with uncertainty ranges. In a blind hindcast it cuts the error of a single global factor by 36%.
The web app delivers this as a burning-activity calendar (year × month) for every country, 4,596 provinces/states, 49,038 departments, or any circle on a 3D globe or 2D map. Users select a region and a date range and download analytics and visualizations (CSV, JSON, PNG report). This gives fire managers, emergency teams and scientists a continuous fire history exactly as MODIS ends. Example: Chilecito, Argentina, July 2026, 31× its usual July.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FireSync answers the questions a fire manager asks every season: Is this month unusual for my area? Which months and years burned most? How does the current fire compare with the past? It shows a burning-activity calendar (year × month) with an accessible color ramp and an anomaly mode versus the historical median. A 3D globe (or 2D map) lets users drill down from the world to a country, a province/state and a department, or draw a circle of any radius. A region + date-range analytics box summarizes any period (total hotspots with likely range, comparison with a typical period, peak month, months above median) and exports CSV, JSON and a PNG report. A ranking shows where it is burning most this month at each level. Every reconstructed value is labelled and carries its uncertainty.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Common filters across sensors: vegetation fires only (FIRMS type = 0), MODIS confidence ≥ 30, VIIRS nominal/high.

2. Reference-satellite chain: Terra → Aqua → Suomi NPP → NOAA-20. Satellites are never summed, so constellation changes cannot inflate counts.

3. Calibration factors per country × calendar month × day/night, fitted on the 2012–2025 overlap and shrunk hierarchically toward country and global factors.

4. Uncertainty from the interannual spread of the factors.

5. Blind validation published inside the app: factors fitted on 2012–2017 predict 2018–2021 VIIRS from Aqua MODIS alone over 6,760 country-months with 22.8% median absolute error vs 35.7% for a single global factor (36% less error), bias −1.7%. Hand-over check on untouched October 2026 data: NOAA-20 reproduces Suomi NPP in 138 countries with 7.7% median error.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Early-warning teams, emergency managers, scientists and land managers keep a consistent 26-year fire history as MODIS ends. The method recalibrates the same way when NOAA-21 or the next JPSS satellite joins. Demo case from the challenge author (CONAE): the Guanchín fire in Chilecito, La Rioja, July 2026: 243 hotspots, +3,140% over the July median, highest July in 26 years, about 11,800 ha burned (MODIS MCD64A1).

TOOLS

C# (aggregation of 45 GB of CSV in ~2 minutes), Node.js (region builders), JavaScript, three.js and globe.gl (3D globe), Canvas 2D (map and charts), Apache ECharts. Boundaries: Natural Earth and geoBoundaries. Hosting: Cloudflare Pages (static, no server, fast worldwide).

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS CONSIDERED

We treat the problem as a continuity system, not a single conversion factor. The app is honest about provenance and uncertainty, publishes its own validation and a MODIS shutdown simulator, works in English and Spanish, on desktop and mobile, and needs no login.
